title: cudaAsync stale page residency after batch coalescing causes sustained GPU memory growth
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Summary: In production Dedicated clusters running continuous batching with KV cache warmup, we observe sustained GPU memory growth over multi-hour windows that does not reclaim after batch drain. Heap/arena metrics indicate pages remain resident in the cudaMallocAsync pool after coalescing and stream syncs complete. This ticket tracks investigation into stale page residency after batch coalescing, hypothesis validation, temporary mitigations, and a safe remediation plan.

Observed impact: Increased OOMs on a subset of nodes when long-lived KV-heavy sequences run mixed small/large batches. Unit cost rises as allocator fragmentation increases and eviction churn amplifies. Customer-facing throughput dips during high-concurrency KV warmups.

Repro steps (stable repro in staging):
1) Run continuous-batching workload with 40 concurrent sessions, mixture of short chat requests (max_tokens=64) and long generation requests (max_tokens=2048) to force mixed batch coalescing.
2) Enable KV-prefetch (prefetch=on) to force early KV allocation and warmup.
3) Observe GPU resident pages and allocator metrics with telemetry: free_bytes, resident_bytes, slab_counts by epoch, cudaMallocAsync outstanding allocations, and stream synchronization latencies.
4) After ~2 hours, note upward drift in resident_bytes that doesn't decline when traffic is dropped to zero and kernel queues are empty.

Key telemetry snippets collected:
- allocator:/gpu0/resident_bytes: +12% over 3 hours, plateaued at new high.
- cudamallocasync:/allocs_outstanding: low (normal), but cudamallocasync:/pools/resident_pages: unchanged after drain.
- stream:/sync-latency: sub-ms but we saw batch coalesce events with postponed async free completion recorded in timeline.
- nvlink and PCIe stats normal.

Hypotheses:
- H1: cudaMallocAsync async free completions are stalled because frees are submitted on a different stream than the owning allocation stream; coalesced batch shutdown delays the stream callback that returns pages to the pool.
- H2: Pool reuse heuristics keep pages pinned as "preferred" for a small-slab-size class after coalescing; a race with KV prefetch keeps a reference alive in staging buffers.
- H3: Continuous batching coalescer merges multiple small allocations into a multi-batch allocator path that bypasses the normal deferred-free queue, leaving pages in a shadow-allocated state.

Experiments run: 
- E1 (Mar 10): Forced explicit stream synchronize on batch completion in staging branch (staging/sync-on-complete). Observed immediate small decline in resident pages but not full reclamation; reduced but still present plateau.
- E2 (Mar 11): Disabled KV-prefetch on subset of cluster. Memory growth rate dropped significantly for matching traffic — supports KV-prealloc reference hypothesis.
- E3 (Mar 12): Toggled cudaMallocAsync pool trimming (set MAX_HOLD_BYTES lower). Reduced steady-state resident footprint but caused small perf regression under cold starts.
- E4 (Mar 13): Instrumented allocation ownership metadata to emit allocation origin (batch-coalescer vs normal path). Found ~37% of leaked pages tagged as "coalescer_origin".

Actionable findings:
- There is a strong correlation between KV-prefetch activity and stale page residency.
- A subset of pages created during the coalescer path are not entering the standard deferred-free completion flow. These pages show an extra "coalescer fence" dependency in the timeline.
- Immediate mitigations (lower pool hold, explicit stream sync on coalescer completion) reduce memory but are not ideal for latency-sensitive workloads.

Temporary mitigations applied: 
- Rollout: incremental config change on Dedicated alpha pool to set pool_trim_threshold_bytes=0 for micro-slabs for 24h (rolled 2026-03-12 03:00 UTC). Observed reduction in orphaned resident pages and improved headroom.
- Feature flag: disable_kv_prefetch_on_high_concurrency enabled for affected tenants as stopgap.

Open questions: 
- Is the coalescer intentionally bypassing deferred-free to optimize latency? If so, what invariant ensures eventual free?
- Can we safely introduce a lightweight completion fence for coalescer allocations that avoids full stream sync?
- Are there kernel/pathological interactions with certain CUDA drivers that delay async free completion callbacks?

Next steps (proposed):
1) Code change: add an explicit non-blocking completion fence for coalescer allocation batches that posts a host-side callback to enqueue deferred frees back to the pool (PR draft branch: runtime/coalescer/async-fence). Target: runtime-1.27.
2) Add allocator-level guard: track allocations where origin==coalescer and if resident for >TTL (configurable e.g., 15m) trigger a reclaim path that performs lightweight trimming.
3) End-to-end tests: create synthetic mixed-batch e2e to ensure no perf regression >5% p95 latency.
4) Driver matrix: reproduce on CUDA 12.x and 12.y kernels (we already saw differences between 12.1 and 12.4 in staging). Add CI job.
5) Postmortem & runbook: document symptoms and temporary mitigations for SRE.

Links & artifacts: 
- Staging dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.local/d/alloc-coalesce/kv-leak-scan
- Instrumentation trace: https://traces.internal/trace/abcd-20260312
- Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2801 (WIP)
- Runbook stub: https://docs.redwood.com/runbooks/kv-coalesce-memory-growth

Acceptance criteria for Done: 
- No unexplained sustained resident growth in 6-hour stress tests with mixed batches.
- New async-fence path validated against driver variations and shows <=2% p95 latency regression on long-tail tests.
- Rollout in canary with telemetry and automatic revert on regressions.

Customer impact: high

Notes: keep this ticket open until post-rollout telemetry confirms fix; follow-up ticket will track allocator refactor if deeper changes are needed.
